$description: CDS Semantic Status Source Set (semantic/status). CANDIDATE, not Stable. Non-visual status meaning roles for the five independent axes of the Semantic Status Foundation Contract. Each token value is the stable technical value identifier; no color, icon, shape, position, motion, aggregate health, consumer, or Product-Profile semantics exist here.

status.$description: Root group of the CDS semantic status vocabulary: five independent axes, five values each (status.<axis>.<value>).

condition.$description: Operational Condition: what state is the subject in, within the declared scope.

nominal.$description: Operates within declared normal parameters in the declared scope; implies no verification, currency, or evidence.

degraded.$description: Operates outside declared normal parameters with reduced capability, performance, or quality.

disrupted.$description: One or more declared functions do not operate; the subject is not fully out of service.

unavailable.$description: The declared function is not provided in the declared scope, regardless of cause.

unknown.$description: The operational condition cannot currently be stated; never a shorthand for nominal.

severity.$description: Severity and Impact: how much the current state matters in the declared scope.

none.$description: No known impact in the declared scope; not automatically a nominal condition.

minor.$description: Impact exists but does not materially impair the declared purpose.

major.$description: Impact materially impairs the declared purpose.

critical.$description: Impact endangers the declared purpose as a whole or creates an unacceptable risk.

unknown.$description: The impact cannot currently be assessed; never treated as none.

confidence.$description: Knowledge Confidence: how sure we are of the status statement itself.

verified.$description: Backed by identified, current verification evidence appropriate to the declared scope.

supported.$description: Rests on relevant but not fully verifying evidence or observation; never rounded up to verified.

uncertain.$description: Relevant indications exist but are incomplete or partially conflicting.

unverified.$description: Not verified; no verification took place or its result is unusable; never displayed as verified.

unknown.$description: The confidence of the statement itself cannot be stated.

freshness.$description: Freshness: how current the observation or assessment is.

current.$description: Recent enough for the declared scope, with a documented observation or assessment time.

aging.$description: Beyond the ideal currency but not yet stale for the declared scope.

stale.$description: Too old to support current decisions in the declared scope; never communicated as current.

expired.$description: Past a declared hard validity limit; must not ground current statements.

unknown.$description: The observation time, and therefore currency, cannot be stated.

evidence.$description: Evidence Availability: whether the statement is backed by accessible evidence.

available.$description: Evidence exists and is accessible via a resolvable evidence identity; availability is not correctness.

partial.$description: Some, but not all, relevant evidence is accessible; the gap stays visible.

unavailable.$description: No evidence for the statement is currently accessible.

not-applicable.$description: Evidence is not meaningfully applicable in the declared scope; requires an explicit recorded rationale.

unknown.$description: Whether evidence exists or is accessible cannot currently be stated.
